profile.name: Nicholas V. Giamblanco
profile.title: Compiler Engineer
summary: I'm a compiler engineer who builds languages, compilers and tooling for hardware accelerators.
These days I design data-flow languages, compilers and debuggers that make unusual hardware easier to program.
My training is in high-level synthesis (HLS): my M.A.Sc. at the University of Toronto, with Prof. Jason H. Anderson, focused on dynamic memory allocation for HLS in LegUp.

experience.role: Senior Member of Technical Staff, Advanced Tech. R&D
highlights: Designing a user-friendly data-flow language and compiler that raises the abstraction level for programming Cerebras' Wafer-Scale Engines.
Built a register allocator that cut code size and improved runtime performance by 40% on average.
Built a methodology to connect and manage hundreds of WSEs at high throughput and bandwidth.
Built a spatial-temporal reservation system for multi-tenancy across many WSEs.
Introduced a hardware debugger for the WSE; deployed R&D tooling to national lab partners (NETL, Sandia).

experience.role: Senior Member of Technical Staff, Strategic Initiatives
highlights: Compiler and runtime optimizations for the world's fastest LLM inference.
Introduced a neural-network-compiler fuzzer for inference and training flows.
Compiled neural networks for a compute-in-memory RISC-V edge device with MLIR and LLVM.
Implemented a path to fully use RISC-V's RVV vector extension.
Hardware design-verification techniques that find bugs up to 16x faster.
Automatic RTL co-simulation environment with up to 76x less simulation time (innovation award).
A compiler infrastructure for hardware static analysis, 5x faster than commercial tools.
Core compiler and runtime features for the Weight-Streaming product, plus a Weight-Streaming tensor debugger.
A replay debugger for the CS-1 with reverse debugging, value tracking and profiling, used company-wide.
Random-program test infrastructure for the LLVM backend; compiler passes that improved code by 10%.
Principal engineer for the LLVM compiler backend, delivered 6 months ahead of schedule.
Sped up an algorithm in a NASA project by 30,000x with high-level synthesis.
